title: John Lennon and Mick Jagger jam in Los Angeles | 1974
content:
Record Plant, Los Angeles
Producer: John Lennon

John Lennon and The Rolling Stones’ Mick Jagger jammed at the Record Plant in Los Angeles on 24 March 1974.

This was a meeting of the drinking group known as the Jim Keltner Fan Club. Also present were Harry Nilsson, Jesse Ed Davis, Al Kooper, Jack Bruce, and Danny Kortchmar.

Lennon produced the session, during which a version of ‘Too Many Cooks (Spoil The Soup)’ was recorded. The song was originally released by 100 Proof (Aged In Soul) in 1969.

Earlier in the evening Lennon and May Pang had attended a fundraiser for actor James Stacy, who had been injured and his partner died when their motorcycle was hit by a drunk driver. The event was held at the Century Plaza Hotel, and in attendance were Frank Sinatra, Liza Minnelli, Clint Eastwood, Cher, and Steve McQueen.
